expectedChanges: Add a town-wide guide metadata layer for duration, moods, guide copy, and manually curated featured works without duplicating WORKS identity or launch data.
Replace the leisure_catalog generic venue menu with a dedicated image-first guide terminal home and reusable carousel for featured, mood, and all-work browsing.
Include open works from both leisure_center and tomogushi_alley when guide metadata exists.
Resolve guide images from assets/works/<workId>/ogp.jpg with icon and text fallback, without adding duplicate image paths to metadata.
Preserve carousel mode and index when a work launched from the guide is closed and return to the same guide state.
Keep existing direct venue launches and return behavior unchanged outside the guide terminal.
plan.promotion: Staging PR and merge only. Production promotion is out of scope.
hqDecisions: The guide becomes a town-wide discovery surface rather than a leisure-center-only catalog.
The home screen exposes three choices only: recommended, browse by mood, and browse all.
Work browsing uses one image-first carousel pattern with previous/next controls and a visible position indicator.
The initial moods are short, play, quiet, and two-player; works may appear in multiple moods.
Featured works are manually curated and are not derived from publish date or popularity.
A work launched from the guide returns to the same guide browse state; works launched elsewhere keep existing return behavior.
v1 does not add swipe gestures, ranking, personalization, search, favorites, or algorithmic recommendations.
alternativesRejected: Keep separate leisure-center and Tomogushi Alley catalogs as the primary discovery model.
Use WORKS array order as the guide ranking.
Duplicate title, venue, launch URL, or image paths inside guide metadata.
Build multiple browse UIs for recommended, moods, and all works.
Add swipe-only or gesture-dependent navigation in v1.
boundaryCases: Zero eligible works shows a simple unavailable message and a back action.
One eligible work keeps the carousel usable without requiring hidden knowledge of gestures.
Previous from the first item and next from the last item wrap around.
A mood with one matching work remains valid.
Open WORKS entries without guide metadata do not appear partially configured.
Guide metadata for non-open or missing WORKS entries never makes those works launchable.
Missing ogp.jpg falls back to icon.png, then to a text-only visual placeholder.
Closing a guide-launched work restores browse mode, filter, and current index.
Launching a work from its physical venue still returns to that venue as before.
testPlan: Run node syntax checks for all changed JavaScript and CommonJS files.
Run tests/test-work-guide.cjs for eligibility, mood filtering, featured filtering, wraparound navigation, image fallback contract, and state restoration hooks.
Run existing town interaction and transition regression tests because main.js return flow is shared runtime.
Use Scope, Risk, and Impact gates against the locked base SHA.
Manually verify the guide home, all three browse paths, launch/close/re-entry, missing-image fallback, and mobile/desktop layout on staging.
plan.problem: The current exhibition guide is a venue-scoped WORKS list whose ordering follows manual newest-first insertion, so it behaves like a catalog/update surface rather than helping visitors choose something to play.
plan.currentContract: WORKS owns work identity, venue, visibility and launch. leisure_catalog is a destination rendered through the generic destination menu, and work-player return state remembers the destination but not a guide-specific browse state.
plan.whyExistingIsInsufficient: The generic menu cannot express a town-wide image-first curated browse flow, mood entry points, or restoration of a carousel position after closing a work without either overloading WORKS or adding guide-specific behavior.
plan.design: Add a separate guide metadata source and a dedicated guide terminal renderer/state module. main.js only delegates leisure_catalog rendering and preserves/restores the guide return view. Existing WORKS launch behavior remains authoritative.
plan.migration: No data migration. Existing WORKS and physical venue triggers remain unchanged. leisure_catalog begins using the new guide renderer when scripts load.
plan.compatibility: Direct work routes, physical venue work launches, Tomogushi Alley menus, leisure-center physical exhibits, and non-guide destination menus retain their existing paths and semantics.
plan.rollback: Revert the implementation commit(s) after the immutable Plan Lock commit. This restores the generic leisure_catalog menu and prior work-player return behavior without changing WORKS data.
plan.promotionRisk: Production is not part of this change. A later promotion must carry only the reviewed staging diff and re-run production safety checks.
